groups.heading: config: hosts was REJECTED, now ACCEPTED
groups.why: The restored zone-index branch is much wider than what zod 3 accepted, so this is a new hole, not the intended compatibility shim. Probed the raw oracle library: zod3's z.string().ip() accepts a %zone suffix ONLY on the fe80 link-local compressed form ("fe80::1%eth0" -> true, "fe80::abcd:1234%eth0" -> true) and rejects it everywhere else ("3d62::9037%eth0", "::1%eth0", "::%1", "2001:db8::1%eth0", "fec0::1%eth0", "ff02::1%eth0", "fe80:0:0:0:0:0:0:1%eth0" -> all false). src/schemas.ts's zonedIpv6 instead accepts any address z.ipv6() likes plus any non-empty zone string, which is exactly why all eight fuzzer examples (5ac3::de2a%wlan0, 2459::52d2%lo0, 7e60::16eb%25, 2001:db8::ff00:42:8329%wlan0, ...) flipped to ACCEPTED - I reproduced each through the merged build. It also newly accepts junk zones: "fe80::1%eth0%bad", "fe80::1%eth0 " (trailing space), "fe80::1%../../etc", "fe80::1%localhost:8080", "::%0" - all rejected by zod3, all accepted now. review/corpus-diffs.md signed off the ip fix on the explicit claim that the union 'reproduces exactly the set zod 3 matched ... nothing new is let in'; that claim is factually wrong, so the sign-off does not cover this. hosts entries are connection targets, so unvalidated zone text (whitespace, a second '%', path-traversal-looking strings) now flows downstream. Action: tighten zonedIpv6 to the form zod3 actually matched (fe80 link-local, zone restricted to something like [0-9A-Za-z._-]+ / %25-escaped), or get an explicit, documented decision to widen. Judgement: the security framing is mine; the acceptance-set facts are probed.

groups.heading: config: timeoutMs was ACCEPTED, now REJECTED
groups.why: Real, undocumented narrowing that nobody has signed off. Probed: timeoutMs = Infinity is accepted by the oracle and rejected by the merged build ('Invalid input: expected number, received Infinity') - zod3's z.number() allowed non-finite values, zod 4's does not. Finite behaviour is unchanged: 1, 0.5, 5000, 1e+308 identical, NaN and -Infinity rejected by both (wording differs only), and an omitted field still defaults to 5000 in both builds. review/corpus-diffs.md covers ip, name and age only and lists nothing about non-finite numbers (the 400-request corpus contained no such value), so this change is outside the human's sign-off. Judgement: unlike the age probes, 'Infinity' is an idiomatic 'never time out' sentinel in JS and Config is assembled in code (JSON cannot express Infinity), so a deployment that passes it would now fail config validation at startup rather than run. That is a product/ops call a human should make and record - either ACCEPT NEW with a note, or accept Infinity explicitly (e.g. a union with a literal sentinel).

groups.heading: signup: ip was REJECTED, now ACCEPTED
groups.why: Same root cause as the hosts group, on the Signup.ip field instead of Config.hosts (both use the shared ipAddress union). Probed each example through both builds: "3d62::9037%1", "::%1", "2001:db8::ff00:42:8329%25", "b87e:5698:6e07:9d7a:f797:88d4:4a6a:3b0f%en0", "dafa::c206%eth0" are rejected by the zod3 oracle and accepted now, because zod3 only allowed a %zone on the fe80 link-local form while zonedIpv6 allows any ipv6 address plus any non-empty zone (confirmed directly against the raw zod3 library). Newly accepted junk also lands here: "fe80::1%eth0 ", "fe80::1%eth0%bad", "::%anything-at-all", "fe80::1%../../etc". The signed-off review asserted the union lets in nothing new, which the probe contradicts, so a human must either tighten zonedIpv6 or consciously accept the wider set. Fixing it once in ipAddress resolves this group, the hosts group and most of the two 'different fields reported' groups.

groups.heading: signup: age was ACCEPTED, now REJECTED
groups.why: This is precisely the change a human already reviewed and accepted: review/corpus-diffs.md section '[2] age - was ACCEPTED, now REJECTED' documents zod 4's .int() meaning *safe* integer with a +/-MAX_SAFE_INTEGER bound, and the sign-off line reads 'ACCEPT NEW on age (unsafe integers now rejected) - agreed', with no code change intended. Probed the boundary and the scope matches exactly: 13, 130, 9007199254740991 accepted by both; 12 and 1.5 rejected by both; only 9007199254740992 and above (and 1e+21, 1e+30, 1.797e+308) differ. Every example in this group is above 2^53, i.e. not a representable age and already lossy as a float. No action needed before shipping; the suggested follow-up (an explicit .max(130)) is already recorded as out of scope for this PR.

groups.heading: signup: rejected by both, but different fields reported
groups.why: Derivative of the ip and age groups, with no independent behaviour change: the API verdict is 'rejected' in both builds for every example, only the issue list differs. I checked all eight examples and each delta is exactly 'ip disappears' (zoned address now accepted) and/or 'age appears' (unsafe integer now rejected); nothing else moves. Reproduced the mechanism directly: 'bad email + zoned ip' gives zod3 [email,ip] vs now [email]; 'bad email + unsafe age' gives zod3 [email] vs now [age,email]; 'everything bad' differs only by the added age. Error wording is deliberately not compared by corpus/canon.js, and a caller still gets the same 400 either way. Judgement: no separate action - these entries shrink automatically once the ip refine is decided, so tracking them as their own bug would be double-counting.

groups.heading: config: rejected by both, but different fields reported
groups.why: Same reasoning as the signup field-set group, on the Config schema: rejected by both builds in every example, so the externally visible outcome is unchanged; only the reported field set moves. Each delta traces to one of the two root causes already flagged: 'hosts.N' dropping out is the zone widening, and 'timeoutMs' appearing is the Infinity narrowing. Reproduced: {hosts:['nope','3d62::9037%1'], timeoutMs:Infinity} -> zod3 [hosts.0,hosts.1] vs now [hosts.0,timeoutMs]; {hosts:[], timeoutMs:Infinity} -> zod3 [hosts] vs now [hosts,timeoutMs]; {hosts:['nope'], timeoutMs:-1} -> identical [hosts.0,timeoutMs] in both. No new acceptance and no new rejection of a whole config here, so nothing to act on beyond fixing the hosts widening and deciding the Infinity question.

groups.heading: signup: website accepted, but the PARSED VALUE changed
groups.why: Judgement call, but no action needed. Probed the scope of zod 4's z.url() output change: it strips leading/trailing whitespace and removes embedded tab/newline (WHATWG URL sanitisation) - ' https://example.com' and 'https://example.com\n' lose the whitespace, and 'https://exa\tmple.com' becomes 'https://example.com'. It does nothing else: case ('HTTPS://Example.COM/A'), explicit port, '/a/../b' path, query order, fragment, userinfo, IDN host and '%7E' percent-encoding all come back byte-for-byte identical in both builds, and acceptance/rejection of URLs is unchanged ('url no scheme' rejected by both). So the only affected inputs are ones containing whitespace or control characters, which zod3 stored raw; the new stored value is the one any URL consumer (fetch/browser) would actually resolve, and dropping stray CR/LF out of a persisted URL is the safer of the two behaviours. 8 of 10000 inputs, all synthetic whitespace variants, and the production corpus contained none. Worth one line in the release notes since it is an output change the signed-off review does not mention, but it needs no code change before shipping.
